description:
Aapki Beti Hamari Beti is a significant welfare scheme launched by the Government of Haryana on 24th January 2016. 

The scheme was introduced to address the issues of gender discrimination and to promote the education and empowerment of girls in the state. 

The primary objective of Aapki Beti Hamari Beti is to improve the sex ratio in Haryana, which has historically been one of the lowest in India. 

As per the 2011 Census, Haryana's sex ratio was recorded at 877 females for every 1,000 males. 

The scheme aims to increase this ratio by encouraging families to educate and support their daughters. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to families for the education of their daughters. 

The scheme provides a financial incentive of ₹21,000 for each girl child born in families that meet the eligibility criteria. 

This amount is disbursed in three installments. 

The first installment of ₹5,000 is given at the time of the birth of the girl child. 

The second installment of ₹6,000 is provided when the girl child reaches the age of one year. 

The final installment of ₹10,000 is given when the girl child reaches the age of 18 years and is eligible for higher education. 

In addition to the financial assistance, the scheme also emphasizes the importance of education for girls. 

Families are encouraged to enroll their daughters in schools and ensure their completion of education. 

The scheme is designed to create awareness about the importance of girls' education and to reduce the dropout rates among female students. 

Eligibility criteria for the Aapki Beti Hamari Beti scheme include that the girl child must be born in a family that is a resident of Haryana. 

Families must also ensure that they do not have more than two children. 

The annual income of the family should not exceed ₹2 lakh. 

This income limit is set to target economically weaker sections of society. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward and involves several steps. 

Parents or guardians of the girl child must apply for the scheme within one year of the child's birth. 

They need to submit the application form along with required documents such as the birth certificate of the girl child. 

Proof of residence in Haryana is also required. 

Additionally, parents must provide income proof to demonstrate that their annual income does not exceed the specified limit. 

The application form can be obtained from the official website of the Haryana Government or from local government offices. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the concerned authorities. 

After successful verification, the financial assistance is disbursed to the bank account of the applicant. 

The disbursement of funds is done through direct bank transfer to ensure transparency and efficiency. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Women and Child Development, Haryana. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the application process and ensuring that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries. 

Contact details for the Department of Women and Child Development can be found on the official Haryana Government website. 

The scheme has shown promising results since its inception. 

As of 2021, over 1 lakh girl children have benefited from the scheme. 

The financial assistance provided has helped families in supporting the education of their daughters. 

The scheme has also contributed to raising awareness about gender equality in the state. 

In addition to financial support, the scheme has led to various community outreach programs. 

These programs focus on educating families about the importance of girls' education and the need to improve the sex ratio. 

The government has also collaborated with NGOs and local organizations to promote the scheme. 

Workshops and seminars are conducted to discuss the benefits of educating girls. 

The scheme has been part of a broader initiative to empower women in Haryana. 

Other initiatives include the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme launched in 2015. 

This initiative aims to prevent female foeticide and promote the education of girls across India. 

Aapki Beti Hamari Beti complements these efforts by providing direct financial support to families. 

The scheme is a step towards creating a more equitable society where girls are valued and educated. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2021-2022. 

This budget allocation reflects the government's commitment to improving the status of girls in Haryana. 

The scheme is continuously monitored and evaluated to assess its impact and effectiveness. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to make necessary improvements. 

The success of Aapki Beti Hamari Beti has inspired similar initiatives in other states. 

The scheme serves as a model for promoting gender equality and empowering girls through education. 

Overall, Aapki Beti Hamari Beti is a comprehensive welfare scheme aimed at improving the lives of girls in Haryana. 

It combines financial assistance with educational support to create a brighter future for girl children. 

The government remains committed to ensuring that every girl child in Haryana receives the support she needs to succeed. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to change societal attitudes towards girls and promote their rights. 

The initiative is a crucial part of Haryana's efforts to achieve gender parity and improve the overall well-being of women in the state. 

As the scheme continues to evolve, it is expected to reach even more families and create lasting change. 

The commitment to empowering girls through education will have a profound impact on the future of Haryana. 

The Aapki Beti Hamari Beti scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to building a more inclusive society. 

It highlights the importance of investing in girls' education as a means to foster development and progress. 

The scheme is a vital step towards ensuring that every girl child has the opportunity to thrive and succeed. 

The government encourages all eligible families to take advantage of this scheme and support their daughters' education. 

By doing so, they contribute to a brighter and more equitable future for all.
